_note: C4 - <pay.Button/>, the wallet button for everyone who is not a Stripe customer (ClosedSource/Documentation/v4-launch/completeness/C4-pay-button.md). The SEVENTH vendor through the inline-native-surfaces law, and the point of the file is that its first three sections are NOT new: sessionRef[], machine[] and retain[] run through the SAME shared core stripe.json pins (@despia/kernel vendor-session.ts / :core VendorSession.kt / Engine/iOS/VendorSession.swift), unchanged. If a vendor ever needs a branch in that core, the family has forked. Only wallet[] is new, and it is new because Core/Pay answers a question no other vendor in the family has: a wallet can be PRESENT AND EMPTY, which is a Set Up button rather than a hidden checkout, and the module already draws that line with `supported` (a card is provisioned) versus `canAddCards` (the wallet exists). wallet[] pins that `auto` never claims a wallet the device cannot use, that an explicit wallet is never silently swapped for another, and that an empty wallet is reported as a SETUP render with a reason rather than as absence. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: the money. The amounts, the currency exponents, the network vocabulary and the sum check are the OTHER shared pure core (payment.ts / Payment.kt / PaymentCore.swift), pinned by OpenSource/Conformance/pay/request.json, and this file does not restate one line of it - the price lives in the session, which is exactly why it is not an attribute on the button.

sessionRef._note: resolveSessionRef(raw), the SHARED resolver. An omitted attribute is the canonical spelling - <pay.Button/> with no session= binds the module's current session and the markup names nothing. The rows below are the ones an author writing a CHECKOUT reaches for: a merchant identifier, a price and a PSP publishable key are all things people paste into markup, and all three are refused. A price in an attribute is the specific mistake this component's contract exists to prevent: the amount belongs to the session, which the module holds, so it never travels over OTA in a document.

machine._note: One session, two views, in wallet words. The overlay face is dsx.module.pay.request (the presented PassKit / Google Pay sheet); the component face is <pay.Button/>. THE DOUBLE-CHARGE GUARD IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS SECTION EXISTS FOR A WALLET: a wallet tap is one gesture away from a real charge, so a tap while the sheet is authorizing is refused `busy` rather than opening a second authorization. Cancellation is not failure and it is not terminal: a dismissed wallet sheet cancels the ATTEMPT and leaves the plan usable, exactly as a declined card does, because telling a customer their card was declined and then refusing to let them try another is the failure mode this law prevents. `notify` includes a button that unmounted mid-authorization - a screen that navigated away is still owed its outcome, and dropping it is how an app charges a card and never says so.

retain._note: The SceneBind keyed-identity law applied to a wallet button. A PKPaymentButton and a Google PayButton are cheap to draw and expensive to be WRONG about: a button that is torn down and rebuilt mid-authorization is a button whose tap handler no longer points at the attempt in flight. The key never carries the session VALUE - keys land in diff logs - and for this module that matters twice over, because the session is the only thing holding the price.

wallet._note: THE ONLY SECTION IN THIS FILE THAT IS NOT THE SHARED CORE, and it exists because Core/Pay answers a question no other vendor in the family has to: a wallet can be PRESENT AND EMPTY. The module already draws that line - `supported` means a card is provisioned and can pay right now, `canAddCards` means the wallet exists and could be set up - and Apple's own marketing guidance says the same thing in UI terms: show the Set Up Apple Pay button when the device supports Apple Pay but has no card, never a payment button that will fail. So `available` is the wallets this surface has at all and `provisioned` is the subset that can pay right now; `provisioned` is a SUBSET OF `available` by construction and the fold never trusts it alone. THREE LAWS: (1) `auto` never claims a wallet the device cannot use - it chooses only from `available`, in the canonical order, and prefers one that can actually pay; (2) an EXPLICIT wallet is never silently swapped for another, because a merchant who asked for Google Pay and got Apple Pay has an integration that does not match their processor; (3) an empty wallet renders `setup` with a reason, never `none` - hiding the checkout from a customer who is one tap from adding a card is the conversion bug this whole module exists to avoid.
